Fit a model and register it in the ledger

pk_run.Rd

pk_run() is the central function of the workflow. It

Usage

pk_run(
  x,
  data = NULL,
  est = NULL,
  note = NA_character_,
  stage = NA_character_,
  id = NULL,
  refit = FALSE,
  cache = c("same_parent", "any"),
  fit_fun = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE,
  proj = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A pk_spec, a pk_candidate (result of the editing verbs, see pk_edit), a run reference, or a run id. For a run, its specification is re-used and the run becomes the parent.

data

Data frame. Default: the registered dataset, see pk_data(). It must contain the required columns (ID, TIME, DV, EVID, AMT); otherwise pk_run() stops before a run is registered.

est

Estimation settings, see pk_est().

note

Free-text description of the run (what changed and why).

stage

Development stage, e.g. "structural", "stochastic", "covariate", "final".

id

Optional run id. Default: the next free runNNN.

refit

Fit again even if an identical completed run exists?

cache

Which identical completed run may be returned instead of fitting: "same_parent" (default) only one with the same parent as the requested run, "any" one with any parent (a cache_hit event records a different requested parent). Ignored if refit = TRUE.

fit_fun

Function f(model, data, est) that returns a fit. Default: the nlmixr2 fit with the strategy of pk_est(). Mainly useful for tests.

quiet

Suppress progress messages?

proj

A pk_project object. Defaults to the current project.

Value

A run reference (pk_run_ref). Use pk_result() and pk_get() to access results and fit.

Details

  1. compiles the specification to nlmixr2 code,

  2. computes the run key from the specification (generated code), the data and the estimation settings, and returns the existing run if the same combination has already been completed under the same parent (caching, see cache; use refit = TRUE to force a new fit),

  3. registers the run (with parent, stage and note) in the ledger,

  4. fits the model,

  5. stores fit.rds, result.rds, spec.rds, model.txt, settings.rds and diag.rds in models/<run_id>/, and

  6. updates the ledger with OFV, dOFV against the parent, AIC, condition number, covariance step status, shrinkage, and the number of flags.

A run that does not complete is recorded with status "failed" and the error message, and the error is re-thrown. This covers an error in the fit, an error while the results are extracted and stored, and an interrupt (the message then says that the run was interrupted). A run is therefore never left with the status "running" unless the R process itself is killed.

The cache respects the lineage. An identical model that was fitted under a different parent is a different step in the development history, so with cache = "same_parent" (default) it is fitted again as a new run. A run that is re-run from itself (pk_run("run003") without changes) returns that run. With cache = "any" the earlier run is returned whatever its parent; the event log of that run then records the cache_hit with the requested parent, so the attempted derivation stays visible in pk_audit().

Examples

# \donttest{
p <- pk_project(file.path(tempdir(), "demo_run"))
d <- pk_data(system.file("extdata", "example_pk.csv", package = "poppkflow"))
r1 <- pk_run(pk_spec(ncmt = 2, iiv = c("cl", "v2")), data = d, est = pk_est(method = "focei"),
             note = "Base model", stage = "structural")
#> → Fitting "run001": Base model
#> Registered S3 method overwritten by 'minqa':
#>   method      from     
#>   print.minqa RcppTrust
#> ✔ "run001": OFV -526.9316, 0 flags
pk_history()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   run_id parent_id stage      description status     ofv dofv_parent n_par   aic
#>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr>      <chr>       <chr>    <dbl>       <dbl> <int> <dbl>
#> 1 run001 NA        structural Base model  complet… -527.          NA     8  224.
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: cov_step <lgl>, cond_no <dbl>, n_flags <int>,
#> #   decision <chr>, decision_reason <chr>
# }
